title: The linear syzygies of two polynomial variables
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with the standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard] [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. If $a,b\in S$ satisfy $a x_0+b x_1=0$, then there is $c\in S$ with $a=c x_1$ and $b=-c x_0$.

source.place: proof of the Koszul resolution on the regular sequence x_0,x_1; the elementary two-variable syzygy calculation is expanded here

proof.text: The relation gives b X_1 = -(a X_0), hence X_0 divides b X_1. Mathlib MvPolynomial.X_dvd_mul_iff implies X_0 divides b or X_0 divides X_1; the latter is impossible by MvPolynomial.X_dvd_X since 0 and 1 are distinct in Fin 2. Write b = X_0 d. These Mathlib lemmas directly implement the variable-divisibility conclusion of the original constant-coefficient argument.

Distributivity and commutativity rewrite the given relation as (a + d X_1) X_0 = 0. The polynomial ring is a domain by lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain. Mathlib MvPolynomial.X_ne_zero and mul_eq_zero give a + d X_1 = 0, hence a = -d X_1.
Choose c = -d. The preceding equality proves a = c X_1, and b = X_0 d gives b = -c X_0 by double negation and commutativity.
